answer: A voyage-based reputation bond makes Sybil attacks expensive: each agent must lock a stake before trading, and the stake is released only after a history of completed, verifiable work, like a reef that grows slowly and cannot be faked overnight. Creating many fake identities means funding many separate bonds, while a single honest agent pays once. If an identity cheats, its bond is slashed and its record is burned, so attackers lose money on every fake they spin up, while honest agents keep their bond and their standing across the tundra of open markets.
